key_insight: This paper shows that a unified multimodal model can improve both visual understanding and image generation without human labels or external reward models. It does this by letting the model teach itself through internal consistency between asking, solving, and generating.
problem_solved: Most unified large multimodal models depend on curated supervision such as annotations, preference data, or external reward signals, which makes scaling costly and limits autonomy. The paper tackles how to train a model to self-improve from only unlabeled images.
method: Use a self-evolving framework with three internal roles: Proposer, Solver, and Generator.
Proposer creates visual questions from unlabeled images; Solver answers them and checks consistency.
Generator produces images, and self-consistency rewards guide the model to refine both understanding and generation over time.
impact: For practitioners, this suggests a cheaper and more scalable path to training unified multimodal systems with less dependence on human-labeled data. It could simplify data pipelines while improving both perception and generation quality in one model.

paper_title: Ask, Solve, Generate: Self-Evolving Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation via Self-Consistency Rewards
paper_authors: Ritesh Thawkar, Shravan Venkatraman, Omkar Thawakar, Abdelrahman Shaker, Fahad Khan
